statement: The trace of an n × n square matrix A, denoted tr(A), is defined as the sum of the elements on its main diagonal: tr(A) = ∑_{i=1}^n a_{ii} = a_{11} + a_{22} + ⋯ + a_{nn}, where a_{ii} denotes the entry on the i-th row and i-th column of A.

symbols.meaning: entry on the i-th row and i-th column of matrix A
dimension (number of rows and columns) of square matrix A

properties.property: Linearity: tr(A + B) = tr(A) + tr(B) and tr(cA) = c tr(A) for all square matrices A, B and all scalars c.
properties.why: Summation over diagonal entries is linear with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication
Transposing a square matrix does not affect elements along the main diagonal

properties.property: Cyclic commutativity of product: tr(AB) = tr(BA) for any m × n matrix A and n × m matrix B.
properties.why: Both expressions equal the sum of entry-wise products ∑_{i=1}^m ∑_{j=1}^n a_{ij}b_{ij}

properties.property: Similarity invariance: tr(P^{-1}AP) = tr(A) for any square matrix A and any invertible matrix P.
properties.why: Direct consequence of the cyclic property tr(P^{-1}(AP)) = tr((AP)P^{-1})

properties.property: Sum of eigenvalues: tr(A) = ∑_{i=1}^n λ_i, where λ_i are the eigenvalues of A counted with algebraic multiplicity.
properties.why: A is always similar to its Jordan form with eigenvalues on the diagonal, and trace is similarity-invariant

assumptions.assumption: A is a square matrix (number of rows equals number of columns).
assumptions.breaks_when: A is non-square (m × n with m ≠ n).

assumptions.assumption: The entries of A belong to a field F (e.g., real or complex numbers).
assumptions.breaks_when: Entries belong to a structure where addition is undefined.

failure_modes.cause: The trace is explicitly not defined for non-square matrices.

failure_modes.mode: Arbitrary permutation of factors in a product
failure_modes.cause: The trace is invariant only under circular shifts (cyclic property), not under general non-cyclic permutations, unless additional conditions like symmetry hold.
